The biologics and specialty therapeutics sector continues to be propelled by aging demographics, rising chronic disease prevalence, and the commercialization of next-generation modalities (e.g., bispecific antibodies, ADCs, and in vivo gene therapies) [4]. Despite strong clinical pipelines, Regeneron faces multiple structural headwinds. Eylea HD’s success will depend less on efficacy and more on manufacturing scalability, specialty pharmacy logistics, and payer contract negotiations that favor extended-interval dosing economics. The oncology franchise faces a "innovation vs. differentiation" paradox: many pipeline assets target established targets with incremental benefits, making real-world adoption highly dependent on comparative effectiveness data and reimbursement alignment.
